system_overview: This specification extends the base EWD998 termination detection algorithm with configurable algorithm variants (feature flags) for statistical efficiency analysis. Unlike EWD998Chan_opts which operates on the channel-based model, this variant operates directly on the abstract EWD998 token model. It defines five optimization variants (pt1 through pt5) and instruments the specification to collect performance statistics written to CSV files.
actors_and_components: The system consists of the same ring of N nodes with a circulating token as EWD998, augmented with feature flags controlling variant behavior. The five feature flags are: pt1 (active node may pass token if node is tainted), pt2 (active node may pass token if token is tainted), pt3 (return token to initiator if node is black), pt4 (return token to initiator if token is black), and pt5 (initiator may only initiate a round when inactive). An additional optimization uses linearly decreasing send probability to encourage termination.
state_variables: All state variables are inherited from EWD998: node activation, colors, counters, pending messages, and token. A TLC register tracks the termination point for delay measurement.
initial_state: Initial states are randomly sampled from the full set of type-correct states to provide diverse simulation starting points while keeping the initial state set manageable.
actions: The specification redefines token-related actions with variant behavior: the initiation action optionally requires the initiator to be inactive (pt5), the pass action extends the pass condition with optional conditions (pt1, pt2) and allows redirecting the token to the initiator (pt3, pt4). Message sending uses linearly decreasing probability to model workload tapering off.
model_bounds: The specification is designed for TLC's generator mode with unlimited depth and no deadlock checking. Node count and feature flags are configured via environment variables.
additional_assumptions: Requires TLC, IOUtils, CSV, and Randomization modules. TLC must run in generator mode with a minimum revision timestamp. Statistics are collected at termination detection points via action constraints and state constraints. The specification validates that action statistics are consistent.
